title: 修复 Weekly Radar 同日完成运行的幂等状态

rawRequestSource.reference: User approved the bounded recommendation after the 2026-08-24 schedule run was rejected because an earlier manual run had already completed the same date.

requestedOperation.authorityReason: The user explicitly approved the bounded workflow correction.
authorizedExternalEffects: Create and update the dedicated Work Item branch and pull request.
Run repository and hosted quality checks without reading Secret values.
Merge the reviewed Work Item through the repository lifecycle.

outOfScope: Adding a new external durable store or artifact protocol for input snapshots created before Telegram delivery.
Reading, printing, copying, or storing any Secret value.
Manual mutation, overwrite, or repair of the data branch and the already published 2026-08-24 artifacts.
Changing source authority, acquisition limits, judgment, ranking, report content, or Telegram transport behavior.
Publishing a replacement report for an already completed date.

sources.reason: The earlier manual run completed PUBLISHED for 2026-08-24 before the later schedule run.
The scheduled run failed with archive already contains a final run after the manual run had completed.
The post-merge manual validation reproduced the same misleading duplicate-date failure before source acquisition.
The non-secret data manifest proves the requested date and bound archive paths.
The non-secret receipt proves the existing archive is PUBLISHED with accepted message IDs.
The CLI currently exposes pending-publication verification but routes an already final date through the duplicate error path.
The existing verifier and fail-closed archive invariants define the safe evidence boundary for an idempotent success.
The existing deterministic report identity is the shared binding needed to validate legacy receipt/report/snapshot consistency without duplicating the digest algorithm.
The runtime facade must export the read-only committed-run verification entrypoint.
The workflow currently treats only PUBLISHED and READY-TO-PUSH as successful outputs and has no already-published no-op path.
Existing tests cover duplicate protection, pending recovery, and published verification but not a successful already-published CLI outcome.
User-facing operations documentation must distinguish completed idempotent no-op, recoverable publication, and fail-closed conflict.
Repository Work Item and production-safety rules.
Canonical AI Cockpit lifecycle and verification commands.

problemStatement: A final successful archive is correctly protected from duplicate publication, but the workflow reports the protection as failure. Operators cannot distinguish a safe no-op from a retryable failure, and a same-date validation run on the merged code cannot provide a clear successful result.

riskAssessment.reason: The change affects a production publication workflow. Risk is bounded by requiring full archive verification before the no-op success, preserving all existing fail-closed guards, adding fixture and workflow regressions, and forbidding data or Secret mutation.
riskAssessment.reviewedBy: Codex after inspection of the three hosted runs, data manifest, receipt, CLI, archive verifier, and workflow.

reasons: A bounded workflow/runtime semantics correction with no provider, Secret, or historical data mutation.

executionDecision.reason: The hosted run evidence, existing archive verifier, CLI, workflow, and tests establish a deterministic and bounded correction with explicit acceptance and recovery boundaries.

preReviewWarnings: The already-published branch must verify all bound artifacts before returning success.
ALREADY-PUBLISHED must never call source acquisition or Telegram and must not create a data commit.
READY-TO-PUSH pending recovery and all incomplete/conflict failures must retain their existing semantics.
The 2026-08-24 historical data artifacts are evidence only and must not be rewritten.
A green no-op run proves idempotent state handling, not a new SEC acquisition for the old date; the next real schedule remains the production validation for the merged SEC fix.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The CLI exposes a verified already-published outcome that validates the complete archive and exits successfully without provider acquisition or Telegram configuration.
The workflow detects a verified final run for the requested date, accepts ALREADY-PUBLISHED, skips Telegram and data-branch writes, and exits zero.
Existing pending publication recovery continues to reuse the original receipt without a second Telegram call, while partial or conflicting state remains fail closed.
Regression tests cover the new CLI outcome, workflow branch, duplicate protection, and existing recovery/fail-closed behavior.
User-facing documentation explains ALREADY-PUBLISHED, READY-TO-PUSH, retryable incomplete state, and non-retryable conflict state.
All declared project and AI Cockpit checks pass without reading Secret values or modifying the data branch.
guidelines: New public CLI behavior must be documented and tested.
Use the existing archive verifier as the evidence boundary; do not duplicate or weaken archive validation.
Keep provider acquisition and Telegram delivery outside the already-published verification path.
Preserve typed fail-closed errors and no-overwrite behavior.
Do not read or record Secret values.
Do not manually modify the data branch or historical production artifacts.

intent.problem: A final successful archive is correctly protected from duplicate publication, but the workflow reports the protection as failure. Operators cannot distinguish a safe no-op from a retryable failure, and a same-date validation run on the merged code cannot provide a clear successful result.
constraints: Preserve immutable final-archive verification, pending artifact reuse, fail-closed conflict handling, and no sensitive-configuration/data-history mutation.
intent.rationale: The existing verification and duplicate guards already protect delivery and archive integrity. The smallest safe correction is to add an explicit verified-already-published outcome and make the workflow exit successfully before any provider call or data write when the requested date is already complete. Existing recovery and fail-closed paths remain separate and testable.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A complete and verifiable final archive for the requested date produces a successful ALREADY-PUBLISHED result.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The CLI verifies report, snapshot, receipt, manifest, and optional input snapshot bindings, then exits successfully without reading provider or Telegram configuration.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add and run a fixture-driven CLI regression with provider and Telegram environment removed.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The GitHub Actions workflow treats an already-published result as a successful no-op.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The workflow accepts ALREADY-PUBLISHED, skips Telegram and data-branch writes, and exits zero after verification.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add static workflow assertions and run the full runtime/end-to-end test suite.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Pending publication recovery remains a no-second-send path.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Existing READY-TO-PUSH recovery behavior and receipt identity remain unchanged.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run the existing pending-ref recovery test and full project checks.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Partial, malformed, conflicting, or unverifiable archive state still fails closed.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The new no-op path never converts incomplete archive evidence into success or sends a duplicate.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run existing archive residue/conflict tests and the new CLI verification test with invalid fixtures.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: User-facing operations documentation explains the status meanings.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Operators are told that ALREADY-PUBLISHED is successful and non-delivery, READY-TO-PUSH is recoverable, and other archive errors require inspection.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Review the documentation diff and run declared AI Cockpit/project quality checks.
